It looks like your message may have been mistyped (possibly due to keyboard slippage or autocorrect). 

Based on the keystrokes, it appears you might be asking:
> **"How many bytes are generated in the world each day?"** (or a question about daily data creation / byte units).

Here is the answer to that question, along with common byte conversions in case you were asking about a specific unit:

---

### Global Data Generated Per Day

* **Daily estimate:** Approximately **3.5 quintillion bytes** ($\approx 3.5 \times 10^{18}$ bytes, or **3.5 Exabytes / ~328 million Terabytes**) of data are created globally every day.
* **Annual estimate:** Worldwide data creation currently reaches roughly **120 to 147 Zettabytes (ZB)** per year.

$$\text{3.5 quintillion bytes} = 3,500,000,000,000,000,000\text{ bytes}$$

---

### Standard Byte Unit Reference

| Unit | Size in Bytes | Size in Decimal / Binary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Kilobyte (KB / KiB)** | $10^3$ / $2^{10}$ | 1,000 / 1,024 bytes |
| **Megabyte (MB / MiB)** | $10^6$ / $2^{20}$ | 1 million / 1,048,576 bytes |
| **Gigabyte (GB / GiB)** | $10^9$ / $2^{30}$ | 1 billion / 1,073,741,824 bytes |
| **Terabyte (TB / TiB)** | $10^{12}$ / $2^{40}$ | 1 trillion bytes |
| **Petabyte (PB / PiB)** | $10^{15}$ / $2^{50}$ | 1 quadrillion bytes |
| **Exabyte (EB / EiB)** | $10^{18}$ / $2^{60}$ | 1 quintillion bytes |
| **Zettabyte (ZB / ZiB)** | $10^{21}$ / $2^{70}$ | 1 sextillion bytes |

---

If you meant to ask something different, please feel free to clarify!
